question: What is the primary purpose of applying a dressing to an open wound?

options.A: To promote healing and protect from infection
options.B: To seal the skin permanently with glue
options.D: To completely stop all cellular activity

explanation: A wound dressing acts as a physical barrier that guards against external pathogens while supporting the natural healing process. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is maintaining a moist wound bed preferred over letting a wound dry out completely?

options.A: Moisture encourages faster epithelial cell migration and repair
options.B: Moist wounds eliminate the need for any cleaning agents
options.C: Dry scabs permanently prevent any scar formation
options.D: Dry environments cause rapid bacterial multiplication

explanation: Cells migrate much easier across a moist wound bed compared to a dry, hard scab, which slows down tissue regeneration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which dressing material is derived from seaweed and used for heavily bleeding wounds?
explanation: Alginate dressings absorb heavy exudate and form a gel, making them ideal for bleeding or heavily draining wounds. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h2)

question: A patient has a shallow pressure ulcer with very little drainage. Which dressing type is most appropriate?
explanation: Hydrocolloid dressings maintain a moist environment ideal for light to moderate exudate wounds like early-stage pressure ulcers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the correct direction for cleaning a wound during a dressing change?

options.A: From the outer edges inward toward the deepest part
options.B: From the center outward to the surrounding skin
options.C: In a random circular motion across the entire wound
options.D: From the bottom of the bed upward to the top

explanation: Cleaning from the center outward pushes debris and bacteria away from the wound bed rather than introducing contaminants into it. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why must sterile forceps or sterile gloves be used when touching the wound bed?

options.A: To prevent the dressing material from tearing apart
options.B: To prevent introducing new microorganisms into the tissue
options.C: To make the procedure faster for the nursing staff
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling any sharp pain

explanation: Open wounds lack the protective skin barrier, making sterile instruments essential to avoid introducing infection-causing bacteria. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h3)

question: What action should the nurse take immediately after removing the old, dirty dressing?

options.A: Touch the wound bed to check for deep heat
options.B: Document the healing progress in the chart
options.C: Remove gloves and perform hand hygiene
options.D: Apply the new sterile dressing right away

explanation: Removing soiled gloves and washing hands prevents cross-contamination before touching sterile supplies for the new dressing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is it necessary to explain the dressing procedure to the patient beforehand?

options.A: To legally transfer responsibility for the wound to them
options.B: To reduce anxiety and gain cooperation during care
options.C: To ensure the sterile field stays open for a long time
options.D: To test whether the patient understands basic anatomy

explanation: Clear communication prepares the patient mentally, minimizes anxiety, and secures their cooperation during a potentially painful procedure. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: Which complication involves the emergency protrusion of internal organs through a wound opening?
explanation: Evisceration is a critical surgical emergency where internal organs break through the separated wound layers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h5)

question: What does skin maceration around a wound usually indicate?

options.A: The dressing material is too dry for the tissue
options.B: Excessive moisture or drainage is damaging the skin edges
options.C: The antiseptic solution was too cold during cleansing
options.D: The wound is healing exceptionally fast with new cells

explanation: Maceration happens when moisture sits on healthy skin too long, causing it to turn white, soft, and break down easily. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h5)
